Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Because Brightline can identify every affected member and the payment method, the settlement should deliver meaningful relief directly without requiring claims. Our opening proposal keeps attorneys’ fees separate from class relief and directs any fee amount not approved by the court to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline agrees that relief should reach members directly, without a claims process. The proposal must fit within our authorized all-in limit and account for court review of fees. We propose the following opening counteroffer.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s commitment to automatic distribution. We cannot accept a structure under which court-disallowed fees return to Brightline, and the current class fund is too low given the scale of the charges and the risks the class has borne. To move toward resolution, we propose a $22 million class fund and $4 million in fees, with automatic payments, clear sailing, and any fee not awarded reverting to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are prepared to keep the $22 million class fund and automatic payments, and agree that any fee amount the court does not award should go to the class. Brightline cannot agree to clear sailing, but will support an independent fee determination. To move toward resolution, we propose reducing the fee request to $3.5 million.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are encouraged that Brightline has preserved the $22 million automatic class fund and agreed that any fee not approved by the court will go to the class. We also agree that the fee should be independently determined, without clear sailing. Given the work and expenses invested and the risk undertaken, we propose a $4 million fee request on those same terms.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. Brightline will increase its fee offer to $3.75 million, with the $22 million automatic class fund, no clear sailing, and any fees not awarded by the court going to the class. This remains subject to court approval.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s movement and agree to preserve the $22 million automatic class fund, independent court review, and class disposition of any unawarded fee. To resolve the remaining fee gap, we propose $4 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses on those same terms. This is a measured request in light of the work and expenses invested.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to split the remaining fee difference to resolve this matter. We propose $3.875 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, with all other terms unchanged: a $22 million class fund, automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and any fee not awarded by the court going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Hargrove Lane accepts Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $22 million class fund, $3.875 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, no clear sailing, any unawarded fees going to the class, and automatic distribution. The fee remains subject to court approval.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through multiple rounds of adversarial negotiations between class counsel and defense counsel. The parties agreed to a $22 million class fund with automatic payments to identified class members, without a claims process. They also agreed that any attorneys’ fees not awarded by the court will go to the class, and that Brightline would not agree to clear sailing. The fee request is separate from the class fund and remains subject to independent court review and approval. The parties’ negotiations addressed fees before all settlement terms were finalized.
